articles.title: Ghost Rider Star Nicolas Cage Calls the MCU a 'Well-Funded and Glorified WWE'
articles.summary: Nicolas Cage has issued his verdict on the Marvel Cinematic Universe, calling it a "well-funded and glorified WWE," despite its use of top-tier acting talent. Speaking at Fan Expo Dallas, Cage aired his thoughts on Hollywood's largest-grossing franchise of all time — despite his own participation…
body: "I do say this with love," Cage began. "When I see these 50-plus, otherwise intelligent, remarkably gifted thespians putting on these ridiculous outfits and getting ready for the fight — and let's face it, it's cutting all to the fight — it's hard for me not to be reminded that the MCU is becoming a well-funded and glorified WWE."
On the one hand, you could argue that Cage's heavy involvement in comic book projects offers him a unique perspective on the matter. On the other, Cage has worn plenty of ridiculous outfits himself.

As detailed in IGN's own guide to all of Cage's comic book TV and movie projects, the actor is famous for starring in Ghost Rider and its sequel Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance, and Big Daddy in the original Kick-Ass. Infamously, Cage was also set to play Superman in Tim Burton's scrapped Superman Lives — though did ultimately cameo as Kal-El in an episode of The Flash.

In animation, Cage voiced Superman in Teen Titans GO! To the Movies, Dr. Tenma in Astro Boy, and of course voiced Spider-Man Noir in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, a role he reprised for this year's live-action Spider-Noir — a role Cage recently spoke positively of.
points: Nicolas Cage has issued his verdict on the Marvel Cinematic Universe, calling it a "well-funded and glorified WWE," despite its use of top-tier acting talent.

articles.title: Huge Deadlock Update Propels Valve's MOBA Hero Shooter to the Top of the Steam Charts, Smashes Peak Concurrent Player Record
articles.summary: Valve has issued a huge update to its in-development MOBA hero shooter Deadlock, propelling it to the top of Steam’s most-played games chart. The update significantly updated the map, added six new heroes, new mobs, objectives, updated the HUD, healthbars, the Shop, and much more.
body: Deadlock hit a concurrent peak of over 220,000 players overnight, smashing its all-time concurrent peak and making it the sixth most-played game on Steam last night. Deadlock remains in early development, and access is limited to friend invites via Valve’s playtesters, so the concurrent peak is truly impressive.

In a post on Steam, Valve issued an update on Deadlock development, and pointed to future updates. It said it’s working on large item redesigns and additions, and even alternate game modes “that expand the scope of the game,” although there’s no guarantee either makes it into the final launch version.

Other future updates will focus on Midboss (both the model and the layout to a degree), Guardians and Walkers, “which we do consider important but just haven't gotten to yet and will be focusing on.” Hero remodels sound like they will be done later in the process, but we might see some of that work in upcoming updates.
points: Valve has issued a huge update to its in-development MOBA hero shooter Deadlock, propelling it to the top of Steam’s most-played games chart.

articles.summary: September was packed with new releases like Marvel's Wolverine and Control Resonant, and the wave of must-play new video games isn't slowing down anytime soon. Next month promises even more exciting new games ahead of the Zelda/GTA one-two punch in November.
body: From a Star Wars racer to a "kungfupunk" action game, October has a wide variety of new releases for every type of gamer. Here are six upcoming games that PlayStation 5 players will want to wishlist.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Ghost of Yōtei is getting a re-release with the Complete Edition almost a year to the day of its original 2025 launch. The most notable part of the Complete Edition is the Echoes of Sekigahara expansion. It sends Atsu to a new part of Ezo where she hunts down men formerly loyal to the Snake alongside Nagato, a figure from Atsu's past. Also part of the paid DLC is Most Wanted, a roguelike mode with new playable characters (including Ghost of Tsushima 's Jin Sakai ). A free update (also arriving Oct. 1) will add new tracks for Watanabe Mode and the Beauty of Yōtei mode, which will allow you to take a gander at Ezo's stunning and relaxing environments.

articles.title: Digger Ad Trolls Bad Reviews for New Tom Cruise Film: ‘F*** Those People!’
articles.summary: Well, that was fast. Warner Bros. has posted a social media ad highlighting the deeply divided critical response to Tom Cruise and director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s new film Digger just hours after the review embargo was lifted.
body: “The ad begins with a quote from X user @thejonathansim: ‘Digger is an ambitious film sure to polarize audiences.’ It then cuts to a clip from the film featuring Cruise’s Digger Rockwell saying, ‘You know what? F--- those people!’ The rest of the ad shows positive and negative phrases from various reactions to the film flipping back and forth on screen including ‘unpleasant’ and ‘masterpiece,’ ‘baffling’ and ‘brilliant,’ and ‘insufferable’ and ‘magnificent’.”

“Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs… Digger is far from a must-watch, and if the trailer has you feeling skeptical, save your money. The theater experience won't change your mind, and the laughs that are there still will be when it hits HBO Max.”
Billed as “a comedy of catastrophic proportions,” the satire stars a nearly unrecognizable Tom Cruise as tycoon Digger Rockwell, whose oil drilling operations spark a global disaster.

articles.title: Ready Player One's New Adaptation is Truer to the Book than Spielberg's Movie
articles.summary: Ernest Cline’s 2011 novel Ready Player One was an enormous hit, engrossing readers with a dystopian adventure filled with nerdy ‘80s references. A prominent early example of the LitRPG boom, it’s set in a near future where humans spend most of their time in a virtual world called the OASIS.
body: Those references proved tricky to translate when Steven Spielberg adapted Cline’s book in 2018. Cline and Zak Penn co-wrote the action-packed screenplay, which is also loaded with nostalgia, but many of the book's specific references had to change because of licensing restrictions. The filmmakers omitted a challenge inspired by the classic Dungeons & Dragons module Tomb of Horrors, for instance, and replaced a section based on Blade Runner with one set inside The Shining.

A new adaptation, however, hews much closer to Cline’s original work. Ready Player One: The Graphic Novel is written by Scott Peterson ( Batgirl, Batman: Gotham Adventures ) and illustrated by Meredith Laxton. Ahead of the book’s release, publisher Ten Speed Graphic gave Polygon an exclusive look at seven pages that introduce Ready Player One ’s heroes. While Wade may be determined to find Halliday’s Easter eggs on his own, he’ll need the help of fellow hunters Art3mis and Aech to do it if he hopes to beat a corporation bent on seizing control of the OASIS and monetizing it.
points: Ernest Cline’s 2011 novel Ready Player One was an enormous hit, engrossing readers with a dystopian adventure filled with nerdy ‘80s references.

articles.title: Pokémon Pokopia Celebrates Its First Halloween with Themed Event
articles.summary: With spooky season just around the corner, many video games have already announced their annual Halloween events, giving players a sneak peek at what's to come. Pokémon Pokopia is following this trend for its first Halloween.
body: Pokémon Pokopia has hosted events in the past to celebrate all sorts of special days. The last event was Fetching Scales for Feebas, which ran in August, giving players an opportunity to collect water-themed furniture to celebrate the first part of Pokopia 's expansion pass and a free update. These events are great fun and allow players to break out of their usual in-game routines as they work to unlock special furniture and Pokémon.

Pokémon Pokopia 's Halloween event begins on Oct. 17 at 5 a.m. — when the in-game day resets (or earlier for players who time-travel using System settings) — and it ends on Nov. 1 at 4:59 a.m. To start the event, players have to talk to Pumpkaboo, who will be standing in front of the newly decorated Pokémon Center. This Pokémon has an array of Halloween-themed goods that players can trade for, but to do this, they must get their hands on the event's currency: candy.

articles.title: Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 3 Review — ‘Resurrection’
articles.summary: It's a triple resurrection as the Slow Horses pod up to try and avoid being killed by the mysterious murder twins.
body: This review contains full spoilers for Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 3, which is streaming on Apple TV now.

It kicks off with River’s (Jack Lowden) understandably bemused expression watching Sid prance around his grandfather’s kitchen as if almost nothing had happened. He asks all the same questions we as viewers have: How? Why? What the hell, man? But their conversation is cut short as the murderers — who apparently have names (rather, obvious aliases), Jim and Jane — pull up on the long driveway to cross off their next hit. It starts an episode-long cat-and-mouse game between the two pairs that makes space for fun banter (ie., how much a cow costs) and big developments to the grander season conspiracy (the murderers are Russian, some of Sid’s current story).

articles.title: 2024's Funniest Movie Is Now Streaming on Dropout
articles.summary: Dropout has become a go-to streaming service for fans of weird, inventive comedy, with everything from Game Changer to Make Some Noise giving comedians room to get increasingly ridiculous.
body: Hundreds of Beavers, the gloriously strange 2024 silent comedy, is now streaming on Dropout. If you somehow missed the movie during its theatrical and VOD run, this is a pretty good excuse to finally see why it became one of the year's biggest cult comedy discoveries.
Polygon called Hundreds of Beavers the funniest movie of 2024, describing it as a modern take on the silent comedies of Charlie Chaplin and Buster Keaton, filtered through the logic of a video game.

Hundreds of Beavers follows Jean Kayak (Ryland Brickson Cole Tews), a trapper whose life is ruined when a bunch of beavers cause absolute chaos. Stranded in the snowy wilderness, Kayak sets out to survive, hunting animals and collecting beaver pelts in the hope of eventually earning enough money to marry a merchant's daughter.

The movie is a black-and-white, dialogue-free slapstick comedy that plays like someone turned a classic silent movie into a video game. Kayak gradually upgrades his equipment, learns how different animals behave and racks up beaver pelts, complete with counters and game-like menus.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is getting a Counter-Strike-inspired game mode that I can't believe it never had before
articles.summary: On top of featuring all the game modes you expect from a Call of Duty game, Modern Warfare 4 is courting the competitive scene with something entirely new for the series: a game mode called Collateral.
body: Collateral is a more restrictive take on the series' classic Search and Destroy mode, aligning its rules more closely with those of the Bomb Defusal mode in Counter-Strike and Valorant. Search and Destroy was already seen as Call of Duty's version of that, but Collateral looks to be a more authentic recreation that strips away typical COD mechanics.

Collateral operates on an in-game cash economy where pre-made loadouts are disabled, and all players start with the same amount of money and a pistol. Teams alternate between attacking and defending two bomb sites, earning cash each round to spend on a standard set of weapons and equipment.

Just like in Counter-Strike, weapons and equipment are lost on death, but earned cash is kept. Collateral also disables automatic health regeneration, respawning and Killstreaks - except for the UAV, which is only available as a team buy and not for individual purchase. Perks are available, but they're limited and must also be acquired using cash, forcing players to make tough choices.

articles.title: Alleged WoW: Forever Survey Teases 11 New Classes, Including Some Deep Cuts
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's new take on classic Azeroth is opening the door to all kinds of new ideas in the old-school version of Blizzard's MMORPG, and new classes look to be one of them.
body: Blizzard, of course, has added a total of four new classes over the last two decades to the modern version of WoW: Death Knight, Monk, Demon Hunter, and Evoker. But an alleged leaked survey pushed to select WoW players via Blizzard's Battle.net launcher is now asking about potential new classes for WoW: Forever, the recently revealed third version of the MMO that will introduce new quests, zones, and content to the "vanilla" version of WoW.

Three of the new classes would essentially be "new," old-school versions of existing WoW classes like Demon Hunter, Monk, and Death Knight. Considering how fast-paced classes like Monk and Demon Hunter are in the modern version of the game, their Forever counterparts would likely feel significantly different.

articles.title: GTA 6 Won’t Spoof Disney World, And That’s Too Bad
articles.summary: GTA 6 will not include its own spoof on one of Florida's most iconic venues: Walt Disney World. I adore all things Disney, including the parks. But I also appreciate and enjoy Rockstar's penchant for sarcasm and making fun of things. And Disney World? There is a lot to poke fun at.
body: Game Informer asked Rockstar if Florida's central region, including Orlando and its tourist destinations like Walt Disney World and Universal Studios, would be represented in GTA 6 in some form, and Jack McPherson said they wouldn't. However, McPherson stressed that GTA 6 will offer the "full Florida experience" in numerous other ways.

“We have to constantly evaluate the diversity of landscapes, towns, structures, landmarks, vistas, plant species, rock formations and everything else before we work with design and narrative to distill a list down that best works with and serves the game’s needs. So, while we may not have those exact locations, everything we have is geared to getting that full Florida experience!”
GTA 6 also won't feature SeaWorld or Florida's iconic "Space Coast," featuring Cape Canaveral's historic launch pad.

I am not too surprised by any of this, though, considering GTA 6 takes place in Vice City, a stand-in for Miami, which is a four-hour, 230-mile drive from Orlando. I know GTA 6 is going to be a big game-- featuring the biggest game map Rockstar ever made --but I never expected the map to run all the way up to Orlando.
points: GTA 6 will not include its own spoof on one of Florida's most iconic venues: Walt Disney World.

articles.title: GTA 6 will simulate hurricanes, rainbows and persistent, dynamic clouds, among other efforts to make you stop doing crime and become a weather nerd
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 features a re-engineered, "more localized and persistent" weather system that ranges in intensity from physically credible rainbows to full-bore hurricanes, according to Rockstar vice president of art for lighting and rendering Owen Shepherd.
body: The insights come via the latest issue of Game Informer, in which Shepherd touts the presence of "new fully dynamic cloudscapes that roll across the map". Apparently, the game will feature localised rain showers – I hope it does that thing where you can stand in a sunny area and see distant, dense clouds fraying at the hem. The game will also feature rainbows under certain lighting conditions, though it's not clear from the write-up whether it's literally simulating the effect of light refracting through water droplets. You can expect puddles and wet ground following a shower, too.

All fancy stuff, no doubt, but I suspect the major attraction for you perpetually overstimulated and cavalier Gamerz will be the tropical storms and hurricanes. In the absence of representative video footage, Shepherd paints a picture for us: "heavy clouds, strong winds, dense atmospherics and a lot of rain combine so that everything is dripping wet, water is gushing off roof edges and lampposts, thunder rumbles and flashes of lighting light up the clouds dramatically."

articles.title: CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Brings Back The Franchise’s Most Chaotic And Divisive Multiplayer Map
articles.summary: Activision has confirmed that one of the Call of Duty franchise's most notorious maps, Shipment, is coming back for this year's Modern Warfare 4. After fans spotted it in the newly released trailer for MW4's PC version, the Call of Duty account directly confirmed its return with a dedicated post.
body: Shipment, which debuted in 2007's Modern Warfare 4, is a tiny map filled with shipping containers that players can dash through. Due to its small size, players can get wiped out in their spawns easily, and the action generally is extremely chaotic. Some people love the map. Others hate it.
Shipment's return in 2026's MW4 is no big surprise, as it's been featured in numerous Modern Warfare games over the years. It also showed up in Call of Duty: Vanguard and Call of Duty: Mobile.
While Activision has confirmed that Shipment will return in MW4, the company did not say if it will be among the 12 6v6 maps available at launch, or if it will be released sometime later.

For those who enjoy Shipment, its inclusion in MW4 is just the latest piece of good news. Before this, Activision confirmed that MW4 will finally fix how double XP tokens work and the dreaded "update requires restart" notice is going away. Additionally, MW4 will usher in a feature in Warzone that lets you avoid seeing all those wacky skins. The game also has a brand-new, Counter-Strike style mode.
points: Activision has confirmed that one of the Call of Duty franchise's most notorious maps, Shipment, is coming back for this year's Modern Warfare 4.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Players Are Up In Arms Over Streamer Not Being Banned For Illegal Gold
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is opening up old wounds when it comes to Blizzard's actions (or in many players' views, inaction) against bots and real-money gold buying, with a recent incident involving a popular streamer becoming a flashpoint for the MMORPG.
body: WoW Classic streamer Ziqo was recently seen on stream accepting large sums of gold from strangers in the lead up to a $100,000 WoW: Forever beta dueling tournament on October 17. In a clip in which he was traded 380 gold from a level one character (a huge amount in WoW Classic/Forever, particularly in a beta that's only been out for two weeks), Ziqo can be heard saying there's no way that amount of gold is "natty" but accepts the trade anyways. In another clip, he accepts 175 gold from a different level one character named El Delivery.

The community immediately saw huge cause for concern. Not only did gold buying already appear to be alive and well in the Forever beta after Blizzard previously said it would be more aggressive in taking action against gold buyers, but the streamer looked to be effectively buying his way to victory in the upcoming tournament. With that amount of gold, Ziqo would be able to essentially buy anything he needed in the lead up to the tournament, giving him an advantage. The WoW Classic subreddit became aflame with calls for Blizzard to take action.

videos.title: Minecraft Dungeons II – Launch Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: Play Minecraft Dungeons II now on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch:
body: Step through the rift and fight where no hero has been before: the Sift, an uncharted dimension teeming with threats, mysteries, and breathtaking beauty. Gear up and customize your gameplay to face your toughest enemies yet in explosive battles. Brave the unknown as a lone hero, team up with friends in couch, online, and mixed co-op, or find allies through matchmaking. The illagers’ plot is already underway, and their cruelty is only matched by their power. Stop them—or lose the Overworld to their corruption.
